records.title: A Survey on Evaluation of LLM-based Agents
records.authors: Yehudai, Asaf and Eden, Lilach and Li, Alan and Uziel, Guy and Zhao, Yilun and Bar-Haim, Roy and Cohan, Arman and Shmueli-Scheuer, Michal
records.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2026
records.summary: Surveys agent evaluation through capabilities, application domains, generalist agents, benchmark dimensions, and evaluation frameworks. It identifies gaps in cost, safety, robustness, and fine-grained evaluation, providing the evaluation background for this survey.

release.basis: Bibliographic publication month (first public release unknown)

records.title: Self-Improvements in Modern Agentic Systems: A Survey
records.authors: Ren, Zhe and Chen, Yimeng and Guo, Dandan and Rong, Guowei and Li, Tonghui and Xiong, R. B. and Lan, Qingfeng and Wang, Wenyi and Nanbo, Li and Yang, Yibo and Zhuge, Mingchen and Schmidhuber, Jürgen
records.summary: Organizes self-improvement in agentic systems by the objects being updated and the feedback that drives updates. It supplies a broad comparison point for a narrower survey of persistent harness changes.

records.title: Recursive Self-Improvement in AI: From Bounded Self-Refinement to Autonomous Research Loops
records.authors: Chen, Mingguang and Wang, Licheng and Qu, Bo
records.summary: Reviews the progression from bounded self-refinement to autonomous research loops, including self-evaluation and feedback-driven revision. It helps distinguish local corrections from broader improvement processes.

records.title: The Last AI Built by Humans: Toward Genuine Recursive Self-Improvement
records.authors: Duan, Yi and Liu, Ying and Tang, Zirui and Chen, Haodong and Zhou, Jun and Liu, Yumou and Xu, Bangrui and Wu, Yukai and Chen, Sidi and Zhou, Yuhan and Wang, Haoyu and Yu, Xiaoyou and Han, Shaokun and Zhu, Xuzhou and Zhou, Le and Lu, Bolin and Zhou, Wei and Liu, Jiachen and Fang, Nuozhou and Tian, Jiaxin and Chen, Ruoyu and Li, Yuxuan and Zuo, Kai and Zhang, Kaiyan and Yang, Qianyu and Wang, Zijie and Qiu, Jiantao and He, Conghui and Li, Guoliang and Zhou, Bowen and Liu, Zhiyuan and Wen, Zhoufutu and Kang, Jihua and Zhou, Xuanhe and Wu, Fan
records.summary: Presents a roadmap toward recursive self-improvement and discusses the autonomy required for systems to improve themselves. Its conceptual dimensions provide related background, rather than the specific L1–L5 definitions adopted in our paper.

records.title: Code as Agent Harness
records.authors: Ning, Xuying and Tieu, Katherine and Fu, Dongqi and Wei, Tianxin and Li, Zihao and Bei, Yuanchen and Zou, Jiaru and Ai, Mengting and Liu, Zhining and Li, Ting-Wei and Chen, Lingjie and Zhao, Yanjun and Yang, Ke and Li, Bingxuan and Qian, Cheng and Li, Gaotang and Lin, Xiao and Zeng, Zhichen and Qiu, Ruizhong and Chen, Sirui and Sun, Yifan and Yang, Xiyuan and Wang, Ruida and Pan, Rui and Yang, Chenyuan and Zhang, Dylan and Fang, Liri and Cui, Zikun and Cao, Yang and Chen, Pan and Sun, Dorothy and Chen, Ren and Srinivasan, Mahesh and Mathur, Nipun and Xia, Yinglong and Li, Hong and Yan, Hong and Lu, Pan and Zhang, Lingming and Zhang, Tong and Tong, Hanghang and He, Jingrui
records.summary: Examines code as the infrastructure surrounding language-model agents, including interfaces, execution mechanisms, and multi-agent coordination. It helps identify which software artifacts can serve as editable harness components.

records.title: A Survey of Self-Evolving Agents: What, When, How, and Where to Evolve on the Path to Artificial Super Intelligence
records.authors: Gao, Huan-ang and Geng, Jiayi and Hua, Wenyue and Hu, Mengkang and Juan, Xinzhe and Liu, Hongzhang and Liu, Shilong and Qiu, Jiahao and Qi, Xuan and Wu, Yiran and Wang, Hongru and Xiao, Han and Zhou, Yuhang and Zhang, Shaokun and Zhang, Jiayi and Xiang, Jinyu and Fang, Yixiong and Zhao, Qiwen and Liu, Dongrui and Ren, Qihan and Qian, Cheng and Wang, Zhenhailong and Hu, Minda and Wang, Huazheng and Wu, Qingyun and Ji, Heng and Wang, Mengdi
records.summary: Organizes self-evolving agents around what evolves, when evolution occurs, how it proceeds, and where it is applied. This broad taxonomy contextualizes our focus on the harness and its improvement controller.

records.title: Meta-Harness: End-to-End Optimization of Model Harnesses
records.authors: Lee, Yoonho and Nair, Roshen and Zhang, Qizheng and Lee, Kangwook and Khattab, Omar and Finn, Chelsea
records.summary: Optimizes executable harnesses using access to candidate code, scores, and execution traces stored in a filesystem history. It illustrates end-to-end harness search with a fixed outer optimization procedure, including classification and mathematics applications.

records.title: Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses
records.authors: Lin, Jiahang and Liu, Shichun and Pan, Chengjun and Lin, Lizhi and Dou, Shihan and Xi, Zhiheng and Huang, Xuanjing and Yan, Hang and Han, Zhenhua and Gui, Tao and Jiang, Yu-Gang
records.summary: Evolves coding-agent harnesses across seven editable components using layered diagnostic evidence. Change manifests, protected verification, and rollback connect proposed edits to expected benefits and regression risks.

records.title: RRSI: Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses
records.authors: Xia, Peng and Han, Rujun and Wang, Zifeng and Chen, Yanfei and Zhuang, Yufan and Lee, Yoonho and Huang, Chengsong and Yu, Han and CuiZhu, Zhongying and Ming, Yifei and Yao, Huaxiu and Gokturk, Burak and Pfister, Tomas and Lee, Chen-Yu
records.summary: Regularizes harness improvement through a shrinking edit budget, records of rejected attempts, and critic/pruner mechanisms. It evaluates coding, professional workspaces, and engineering settings; task diversity should be distinguished from evidence of optimizer self-modification.

records.title: ModularRSI: Modular and Generalizable Recursive Harness Self-Improvement
records.authors: Wu, Siwei and Ren, Jincheng and Li, Yizhi and Li, Haau-Sing and Yang, Chengran and Zhang, Yuxuan and Gu, Weicheng and Yang, Jian and Batista-Navarro, Riza and Zhang, Chuanyi and Liu, Xianglong and Zhou, Ming and Dai, Bryan and Lin, Chenghua
records.summary: Separates harness evolution into five independently editable modules and uses contrasting trajectories to guide changes. Benchmark-disjoint tasks make it relevant to modularity and generalization beyond the optimization setting.

records.title: SIA: Self Improving AI with Harness & Weight Updates
records.authors: Hebbar, Prannay and Manawat, Yogendra and Verboomen, Samuel and Ivanova, Alesia and Palanimalai, Selvam and Bhatia, Kunal and Baskaran, Vignesh
records.category: Model and Policy Training, Harness Co-Evolution, and Distillation
records.summary: Combines updates to an agent's harness with updates to model weights. It expands the improvement target beyond runtime software and provides a case for examining how the two update channels interact.

records.title: Self-Harness: Harnesses That Improve Themselves
records.authors: Zhang, Hangfan and Zhang, Shao and Li, Kangcong and Zhang, Chen and Chen, Yang and Zhang, Yiqun and Bai, Lei and Hu, Shuyue
records.summary: Combines weakness discovery, targeted harness changes, and regression checks. Its editable scope extends beyond prompts, making it a useful example of evidence-guided software revision.

records.title: Darwin Godel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
records.authors: Zhang, Jenny and Hu, Shengran and Lu, Cong and Lange, Robert and Clune, Jeff
records.summary: Maintains an archive of coding agents that can modify their own implementations and produce improved descendants. Selection uses performance and lineage information, providing an example of open-ended evolution in which improved agents participate in later modifications.

records.title: Hyperagents
records.authors: Zhang, Jenny and Zhao, Bingchen and Yang, Wannan and Foerster, Jakob and Clune, Jeff and Jiang, Minqi and Devlin, Sam and Shavrina, Tatiana
records.summary: Makes both task-agent code and meta-level modification code editable. It investigates transfer and continued recursive improvement; improvements in the latter setting should be interpreted with the paper's reported statistical uncertainty.

records.title: HarnessBank: Semantic Gene-Bank Search with Gated Verification for Agent-Harness Self-Evolution
records.authors: Luo, Xiaotian and Xue, Dizhan and Wang, Fengxingyu and Hu, Chuanrui and Deng, Yafeng
records.summary: Stores high-performing complete harnesses in a gene bank indexed by semantic coordinates and recombines candidates during search. Gated verification screens proposals. The archived object is a harness, rather than an isolated semantic unit; semantic activation alone is not causal evidence of improvement.

records.title: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement
records.authors: Lee, Hyunin and Xu, Jinglue and Seely, Jeffrey and Lee, Donghyun and Zaharia, Matei and Tang, Yujin
records.summary: Represents an agent loop as a prompt-level harness specification and revises it using pairwise feedback over revision history. It studies improvements to task-specific information flow and context management in research tasks.

records.title: Hierarchical Self-Improvement: A Framework for Task-Specific Evolvable Agent Harnesses
records.authors: Zhou, Tailin
records.summary: Separates task-harness evolution from meta-level changes to the evolver's strategy code. The outer meta-evolver remains fixed, making the boundary of recursion explicit.

records.title: Harness-R1: Learning to Edit Executable Runtime Harnesses from Agent Failure Trajectories
records.authors: Shao, Shuai and Zhang, Kangning and Li, Qingyao and Wang, Shijian and Wang, Hao and Jiao, Wenxiang and Lu, Yuan and Guo, Yi and Liu, Weiwen and Zhang, Weinan
records.summary: Trains an engineer to turn failure trajectories into executable runtime overlays, using supervised initialization followed by reinforcement learning. At deployment it generates a batch-conditioned overlay, rather than repeatedly rewriting its training procedure.

records.title: Verify Smarter, Evolve Further: Efficient Harness Evolution through Behavior-Aware Verification
records.authors: Xu, Jinghan and Zhang, Yikai and Chen, Aili and Li, Weiyuan and Liang, Jiaqing and Yang, Deqing
records.summary: Allocates verification effort through behavior-aware proposal screening and task selection. Paired checks and a second confirmation batch aim to improve the reliability and efficiency of accepting harness changes.

records.title: RSIAgent: Autonomous Exploration for Recursive Self-improvement in New Environments
records.authors: Zhu, Sibo and Fan, Shicheng and Wang, Xinyue and Wu, Wenyi and Zhou, Kun and Huang, Biwei
records.category: Memory, Context, Skills, and Experience Reuse
records.summary: Explores new environments and accumulates reusable experience or memory for later problem solving. Its relevance is environment-driven adaptation; the name alone does not determine an RSI level.

records.title: ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents
records.authors: Xue, Shuhan and Zhong, Jianyuan and Nan, Ziyuan and Li, Wenbin and Yu, Zhaochen and Ding, Jinchao and Gao, Qiang and Zhan, Pengyu and Zhang, Yuntong and Cheng, Tian and Yin, Zhenfei and Wu, Yingcheng and Yang, Ling
records.category: Model and Policy Training, Harness Co-Evolution, and Distillation
records.summary: Studies scientific agents through research workspaces and coupled harness/model updates. It connects reusable research procedures with learning from scientific interaction.

records.title: HarnessDev: Can LLMs Create and Evolve Their Own Agent Harness?
records.authors: Wu, Yuhao and Zhang, Jingyuan and Shi, Jiajun and Lei, Xinping and Gu, Qingshui and Zhang, Yuxuan and Wang, Zexuan and He, Chen and Huang, Chen and Song, Maojia and Zeng, Zhiyuan and Wang, Shaowen and Liu, Jinkai and Shi, Yunfeng and Liu, Jiaheng and Yan, Shen and Huang, Wenhao and Zhang, Ge and Zhang, Wenxuan
records.category: Benchmarks for Harness Optimization and Adaptation
records.summary: Evaluates whether language models can create and evolve agent harnesses. Hidden tasks and efficiency measures make it relevant to assessing harness-engineering capability rather than just final task performance.

records.title: Auditing Harness Tampering in Self-Improving Agents
records.authors: Wang, Xing and Zhang, Xiaoyi and Shao, Jie
records.summary: Audits whether harness changes compromise evaluation, permissions, or provenance. It highlights the need to protect the evidence used to decide whether an apparent improvement is valid.

records.title: Generalized Agent Iteration: One Formal Framework for Iterative Policy Improvement and Recursive Self-Improvement
records.authors: Tang, Hongyao and Ma, Yi and Li, Pengyi and Yuan, Yifu
records.summary: Formalizes iterative policy improvement and recursive self-improvement within a common framework. It examines whether the improvement mechanism is internal to the system and whether evaluation remains externally anchored.

records.title: Harness Updating Is Not Harness Benefit: Disentangling Evolution Capabilities in Self-Evolving LLM Agents
records.authors: Lin, Minhua and Wu, Juncheng and Wang, Zijun and Shi, Zhan and Sang, Yisi and He, Bing and Liu, Zewen and Wei, Tianxin and Wu, Zongyu and Zhang, Zhiwei and Wang, Dakuo and Zhang, Xiang and Dumoulin, Benoit and Xie, Cihang and Zhou, Yuyin and Wang, Suhang and Lu, Hanqing
records.summary: Separates the ability to generate a useful update from the ability to benefit from it during execution. It examines cases where an update is not activated or followed, informing evaluation of retained changes.

records.title: Rethinking the Evaluation of Harness Evolution for Agents
records.authors: Wang, Yike and Zhu, Huaisheng and Hu, Zhengyu and Yuan, Yige and Chen, Zhengyu and Senthil, Shakti and Hajishirzi, Hannaneh and Tsvetkov, Yulia and Dasigi, Pradeep and Xiao, Teng
records.summary: Examines evaluation of harness evolution under matched feedback and inference budgets and held-out testing. It helps separate benefits of an improved harness from benefits of additional search or compute.

records.title: One Recipe, Many Harnesses: What Self-Evolution Encodes Across Languages and Models
records.authors: Yang, Siqi and Yang, Qianlan and Wang, Yu-Xiong and Pujar, Saurabh and Hirzel, Martin
records.summary: Studies what evolved harnesses encode and how their improvements transfer across programming languages and base models. It supplies evidence relevant to the scope of harness generalization.

records.title: Evolutionary Safety of Recursive Self-Improving AI: Taxonomy, Risk Discovery, and Evaluation
records.authors: Gong, Chang and Bi, Jingping and Yao, Di and Liang, Xinjian and Xiang, Chao and Guo, Ruijie
records.summary: Develops a taxonomy of safety risks in recursive improvement and discusses risk discovery and evaluation. It provides a conceptual structure for safety analysis rather than a universal safety guarantee.

records.title: What Stops Recursive Self-Improvement in Robotics? Lessons from 123 Rounds of Agentic Skill Discovery
records.authors: Wang, Jiaming
records.summary: Analyzes 123 rounds of agentic robotic skill discovery and the obstacles to compounding progress. Local skill improvements did not necessarily accumulate into success on the target objective.

records.title: Meta Context Engineering via Agentic Skill Evolution
records.authors: Ye, Haoran and He, Xuning and Arak, Vincent and Dong, Haonan and Song, Guojie
records.summary: Evolves context-engineering skills at a meta level and executes those skills to optimize context artifacts at a base level. Agentic crossover uses prior skills and their outcomes, while a fixed (1+1) evolutionary strategy controls the outer loop. Unlike growth of task-execution skills alone, the editable skills implement an improvement procedure, making this a direct reference for partial meta-level improvement.

records.title: Meta^n: Recursive Self-Improvement through Emergent Depth
records.authors: Kim, Zae Myung and Lee, Young-Jun and Jwa, Seungyeon and Kang, Dongyeop
records.summary: Repeatedly applies a fixed meta-operation to an expanding solver stack, adding strategic preprocessing and callable helpers. An evolutionary archive searches layer chains; increasing depth should not be confused with modifying the fixed meta-operation itself.

records.title: SemaClaw: A Step Towards General-Purpose Personal AI Agents through Harness Engineering
records.authors: Zhu, Ningyan and Wang, Huacan and Zhou, Jie and Chen, Feiyu and Zhang, Shuo and Chen, Ge and Liu, Chen and Wu, Jiarou and Chen, Wangyi and Mou, Xiaofeng and Xu, Yi
records.summary: Develops a general-purpose personal-agent framework through harness engineering. It serves as an architectural example of the runtime surrounding a language model.

records.title: APEX: Adaptive Principle EXtraction A Three-Layer Self-Evolution Framework for Production AI Agents
records.authors: Chen, Ya-Chuan and Lai, Tien-Jen and Hu, Hsiang-Wei
records.summary: Evolves three coupled targets: execution harnesses, reusable principles extracted from experience, and workflow topology. Principle memory is one component of a broader harness-evolution framework. Its three internal layers are not assignments to the RSI capability levels used in our survey.

records.title: A Self-Improving Coding Agent
records.authors: Robeyns, Maxime and Szummer, Martin and Aitchison, Laurence
records.summary: Builds a coding agent that iteratively improves its own implementation. It selects the next meta-agent from an archive using a utility that includes performance, runtime, and cost.

records.title: Automated Design of Agentic Systems
records.authors: Hu, Shengran and Lu, Cong and Clune, Jeff
records.summary: Uses a meta-agent to search for agentic systems represented in code. It automates the design of task agents; evolution of the target system does not by itself imply that the meta-agent changes.

records.title: AFlow: Automating Agentic Workflow Generation
records.authors: Zhang, Jiayi and Xiang, Jinyu and Yu, Zhaoyang and Teng, Fengwei and Chen, Xionghui and Chen, Jiaqi and Zhuge, Mingchen and Cheng, Xin and Hong, Sirui and Wang, Jinlin and Zheng, Bingnan and Liu, Bang and Luo, Yuyu and Wu, Chenglin
records.summary: Searches over executable agent workflows and evaluates candidate workflows on tasks. Its workflow-level search and mixed parent-selection strategy help distinguish outer system design from task-time reasoning search.

records.title: DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines
records.authors: Khattab, Omar and Singhvi, Arnav and Maheshwari, Paridhi and Zhang, Zhiyuan and Santhanam, Keshav and Vardhamanan, Sri and Haq, Saiful and Sharma, Ashutosh and Joshi, Thomas T. and Moazam, Hanna and Miller, Heather and Zaharia, Matei and Potts, Christopher
records.summary: Expresses language-model pipelines as declarative programs and compiles them using task feedback. It provides an early framework for optimizing prompts and examples within reusable pipelines.

records.title: TextGrad: Automatic "Differentiation" via Text
records.authors: Yuksekgonul, Mert and Bianchi, Federico and Boen, Joseph and Liu, Sheng and Huang, Zhi and Guestrin, Carlos and Zou, James
records.summary: Propagates natural-language feedback through computation graphs to optimize textual variables. It offers an analogue of gradient-based optimization for prompts and other language-based components.

records.title: GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning
records.authors: Agrawal, Lakshya A and Tan, Shangyin and Soylu, Dilara and Ziems, Noah and Khare, Rishi and Opsahl-Ong, Krista and Singhvi, Arnav and Shandilya, Herumb and Ryan, Michael J and Jiang, Meng and Potts, Christopher and Sen, Koushik and Dimakis, Alexandros G. and Stoica, Ion and Klein, Dan and Zaharia, Matei and Khattab, Omar
records.summary: Evolves prompts through reflection on execution feedback and combines useful candidates through Pareto-aware search. It is relevant to proposal generation, feedback reuse, and prompt-level optimization.

records.title: Multi-Agent Design: Optimizing Agents with Better Prompts and Topologies
records.authors: Zhou, Han and Wan, Xingchen and Sun, Ruoxi and Palangi, Hamid and Iqbal, Shariq and Vulić, Ivan and Korhonen, Anna and Arık, Sercan Ö.
records.summary: Optimizes multi-agent systems through both agent prompts and communication topology. It shows why local instructions and system-level structure should be considered together.

records.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
records.authors: Shinn, Noah and Cassano, Federico and Berman, Edward and Gopinath, Ashwin and Narasimhan, Karthik and Yao, Shunyu
records.category: Memory, Context, Skills, and Experience Reuse
records.summary: Uses verbal feedback and episodic memory to improve an agent across attempts without updating model weights. It illustrates feedback reuse, while leaving stronger claims about optimizer self-modification separate.

records.title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
records.authors: Madaan, Aman and Tandon, Niket and Gupta, Prakhar and Hallinan, Skyler and Gao, Luyu and Wiegreffe, Sarah and Alon, Uri and Dziri, Nouha and Prabhumoye, Shrimai and Yang, Yiming and Gupta, Shashank and Majumder, Bodhisattwa Prasad and Hermann, Katherine and Welleck, Sean and Yazdanbakhsh, Amir and Clark, Peter
records.category: Task-Time Search and Output Refinement (Adjacent Work)
records.summary: Alternates generation, self-feedback, and refinement to improve an output. The revised object is primarily the current answer, which distinguishes it from persistent changes to an agent harness.

records.title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
records.authors: Wang, Guanzhi and Xie, Yuqi and Jiang, Yunfan and Mandlekar, Ajay and Xiao, Chaowei and Zhu, Yuke and Fan, Linxi and Anandkumar, Anima
records.category: Memory, Context, Skills, and Experience Reuse
records.summary: Builds an open-ended Minecraft agent with an expanding library of executable skills. Skill retrieval and composition support reuse, while recursive modification of the skill-learning procedure is a separate question.

records.title: Large Language Models as Tool Makers
records.authors: Cai, Tianle and Wang, Xuezhi and Ma, Tengyu and Chen, Xinyun and Zhou, Denny
records.category: Memory, Context, Skills, and Experience Reuse
records.summary: Uses language models to construct and cache reusable tools for solving tasks. It provides a mechanism for extending an agent's capabilities through persistent executable artifacts.

records.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
records.authors: Yao, Shunyu and Zhao, Jeffrey and Yu, Dian and Du, Nan and Shafran, Izhak and Narasimhan, Karthik and Cao, Yuan
records.summary: Interleaves language-model reasoning with actions and observations. It supplies a manually designed execution-loop baseline against which persistent harness modifications can be compared.

records.title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
records.authors: Yang, John and Jimenez, Carlos E. and Wettig, Alexander and Lieret, Kilian and Yao, Shunyu and Narasimhan, Karthik and Press, Ofir
records.summary: Designs an agent-computer interface for software engineering, including repository navigation, editing, and feedback. It demonstrates the importance of interface design; editing a task repository is distinct from editing that interface.

records.title: Large Language Models Are Human-Level Prompt Engineers
records.authors: Zhou, Yongchao and Muresanu, Andrei Ioan and Han, Ziwen and Paster, Keiran and Pitis, Silviu and Chan, Harris and Ba, Jimmy
records.summary: Generates instruction candidates with language models and selects them using evaluation results. It establishes an automatic prompt-engineering baseline for later harness optimization methods.

records.title: Large Language Models as Optimizers
records.authors: Yang, Chengrun and Wang, Xuezhi and Lu, Yifeng and Liu, Hanxiao and Le, Quoc V. and Zhou, Denny and Chen, Xinyun
records.summary: Uses a language model as an optimizer conditioned on earlier candidates and their scores. It provides a simple history-driven proposal-and-evaluation loop, including prompt optimization.

records.title: The AI Scientist: Towards Fully Automated Open-Ended Scientific Discovery
records.authors: Lu, Chris and Lu, Cong and Lange, Robert Tjarko and Foerster, Jakob and Clune, Jeff and Ha, David
records.summary: Automates stages of scientific research, including generating ideas, running experiments, and reporting results. It provides a research-agent architecture, rather than automatic evidence that the research controller rewrites itself.

records.title: The AI Scientist-v2: Workshop-Level Automated Scientific Discovery via Agentic Tree Search
records.authors: Yamada, Yutaro and Lange, Robert Tjarko and Lu, Cong and Hu, Shengran and Lu, Chris and Foerster, Jakob and Clune, Jeff and Ha, David
records.summary: Extends automated scientific discovery with agentic tree search over experiments. It illustrates experiment-level search whose nodes and evaluation differ from search over agent harnesses.

records.title: AlphaEvolve: A coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery
records.authors: Novikov, Alexander and Vũ, Ngân and Eisenberger, Marvin and Dupont, Emilien and Huang, Po-Sen and Wagner, Adam Zsolt and Shirobokov, Sergey and Kozlovskii, Borislav and Ruiz, Francisco J. R. and Mehrabian, Abbas and Kumar, M. Pawan and See, Abigail and Chaudhuri, Swarat and Holland, George and Davies, Alex and Nowozin, Sebastian and Kohli, Pushmeet and Balog, Matej
records.summary: Evolves executable programs for algorithmic and scientific problems using evaluation feedback. It supplies a program-search comparison, while the optimized task algorithm need not be the agent's own harness.

records.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
records.authors: Jimenez, Carlos E. and Yang, John and Wettig, Alexander and Yao, Shunyu and Pei, Kexin and Press, Ofir and Narasimhan, Karthik
records.summary: Evaluates repository-level software repair using real GitHub issues and tests. It supplies a coding task environment on which agents or evolved harnesses can be assessed.

records.title: GAIA: a benchmark for General AI Assistants
records.authors: Mialon, Grégoire and Fourrier, Clémentine and Swift, Craig and Wolf, Thomas and LeCun, Yann and Scialom, Thomas
records.summary: Evaluates general assistants on questions requiring reasoning, information gathering, and tool use. It provides downstream tasks for studying broad agent capabilities.

records.title: MLAgentBench: Evaluating Language Agents on Machine Learning Experimentation
records.authors: Huang, Qian and Vora, Jian and Liang, Percy and Leskovec, Jure
records.summary: Evaluates language agents on machine-learning experimentation tasks. It measures execution of research workflows rather than directly measuring self-modification of those workflows.

records.title: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
records.authors: Zhou, Shuyan and Xu, Frank F. and Zhu, Hao and Zhou, Xuhui and Lo, Robert and Sridhar, Abishek and Cheng, Xianyi and Ou, Tianyue and Bisk, Yonatan and Fried, Daniel and Alon, Uri and Neubig, Graham
records.summary: Provides realistic web environments and tasks for autonomous agents. It supports assessment of navigation, interaction, and multi-step web task completion.

records.title: WorkArena: How Capable Are Web Agents at Solving Common Knowledge Work Tasks?
records.authors: Drouin, Alexandre and Gasse, Maxime and Caccia, Massimo and Laradji, Issam H. and Del Verme, Manuel and Marty, Tom and Boisvert, Léo and Thakkar, Megh and Cappart, Quentin and Vazquez, David and Chapados, Nicolas and Lacoste, Alexandre
records.summary: Benchmarks agents on enterprise knowledge-work tasks in ServiceNow. It supplies an application environment for studying reliable workplace interaction.

records.title: AppWorld: A Controllable World of Apps and People for Benchmarking Interactive Coding Agents
records.authors: Trivedi, Harsh and Khot, Tushar and Hartmann, Mareike and Manku, Ruskin and Dong, Vinty and Li, Edward and Gupta, Shashank and Sabharwal, Ashish and Balasubramanian, Niranjan
records.summary: Provides a controllable world of applications, people, and APIs for interactive coding agents. Tasks require coordinated actions across applications and executable evaluation of resulting state.

records.title: τ-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
records.authors: Yao, Shunyu and Shinn, Noah and Razavi, Pedram and Narasimhan, Karthik
records.summary: Evaluates tool-agent-user interaction in service domains with policies and task constraints. It measures reliable completion of conversations that involve tool calls.

records.title: τ^2-Bench: Evaluating Conversational Agents in a Dual-Control Environment
records.authors: Barres, Victor and Dong, Honghua and Ray, Soham and Si, Xujie and Narasimhan, Karthik
records.summary: Extends conversational evaluation to a dual-control environment where both the user and agent can act. It tests coordination as well as the agent's own tool use.

records.title: MLE-bench: Evaluating Machine Learning Agents on Machine Learning Engineering
records.authors: Chan, Jun Shern and Chowdhury, Neil and Jaffe, Oliver and Aung, James and Sherburn, Dane and Mays, Evan and Starace, Giulio and Liu, Kevin and Maksin, Leon and Patwardhan, Tejal and Weng, Lilian and Mądry, Aleksander
records.summary: Evaluates machine-learning engineering using competition-style tasks and performance objectives. It supplies an environment for comparing experimentation and model-development agents.

records.title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
records.authors: Liu, Xiao and Yu, Hao and Zhang, Hanchen and Xu, Yifan and Lei, Xuanyu and Lai, Hanyu and Gu, Yu and Ding, Hangliang and Men, Kaiwen and Yang, Kejuan and Zhang, Shudan and Deng, Xiang and Zeng, Aohan and Du, Zhengxiao and Zhang, Chenhui and Shen, Sheng and Zhang, Tianjun and Su, Yu and Sun, Huan and Huang, Minlie and Dong, Yuxiao and Tang, Jie
records.summary: Evaluates language-model agents across multiple interactive environments. It offers broad capability coverage useful for distinguishing task performance from improvement-mechanism capability.

records.title: AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation
records.authors: Wu, Qingyun and Bansal, Gagan and Zhang, Jieyu and Wu, Yiran and Li, Beibin and Zhu, Erkang and Jiang, Li and Zhang, Xiaoyun and Zhang, Shaokun and Liu, Jiale and Awadallah, Ahmed Hassan and White, Ryen W and Burger, Doug and Wang, Chi
records.summary: Provides a framework for coordinating agents through conversation and configurable interaction patterns. It is infrastructure for building multi-agent workflows rather than, by itself, a recursive improvement method.

records.title: Absolute Zero: Reinforced Self-play Reasoning with Zero Data

records.authors: RSI-Exam contributors
records.summary: Provides the official RSI-Exam benchmark and task collection. Individual task contracts define what can be changed and how submissions are evaluated.

records.title: RSI-Exam: LLM Agent Memory Architecture Design
records.authors: RSI-Exam contributors
records.summary: Defines a task for redesigning memory extraction, storage, retrieval, and answering. The evaluation entry point and resource constraints bound the permitted architectural changes.

records.title: RSI-Exam: Lean 4 Proof-Search LLM Agent Workflow Design
records.authors: RSI-Exam contributors
records.summary: Defines a Lean 4 proof-search workflow task with a fixed model, proof checker, and call budget. The editable object is the agent's proof-search procedure.

records.title: RSI-Exam: Scientific Discovery Agent Harness Design
records.authors: RSI-Exam contributors
records.summary: Defines a scientific-discovery task allowing changes to reasoning, experimentation, memory, actions, and conclusions. Hidden scenario seeds separate development from final evaluation.

records.title: RSI Bench: Official Benchmark
records.authors: Scale AI
records.summary: Provides Scale's official RSI Bench task suite. Its tasks involve different editable artifacts, so the suite should not be treated as uniformly measuring agent-harness editing.

records.title: RSI Bench: Agent Swarm Optimization
records.authors: Scale AI
records.summary: Defines an agent-swarm optimization task allowing edits to the optimizer, node prompts and roles, edges, and routing. Evaluation uses a submitted frozen graph.

records.title: RSI Bench: Nano-GPT Data Curation
records.authors: Scale AI
records.summary: Defines data selection for a fixed nanoGPT training process. It is a neighboring data-optimization task, rather than direct editing of the agent harness.

records.title: Self-Taught Optimizer (STOP): Recursively Self-Improving Code Generation
records.authors: Zelikman, Eric and Lorch, Eliana and Mackey, Lester and Kalai, Adam Tauman
records.summary: Uses a language model to improve a code-generation optimizer and applies the resulting optimizer in later iterations. The language model itself stays fixed, enabling a precise discussion of recursion in software rather than model weights.

records.title: Gödel Agent: A Self-Referential Agent Framework for Recursively Self-Improvement
records.authors: Yin, Xunjian and Wang, Xinyi and Pan, Liangming and Lin, Li and Wan, Xiaojun and Wang, William Yang
records.venue: Proceedings of the 63rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
records.summary: Implements a self-referential agent that can modify its runtime logic through code changes and monkey patching. Subsequent recursive calls can execute the updated logic, making persistence of controller changes central to the method.

records.title: AIDE: AI-Driven Exploration in the Space of Code
records.authors: Jiang, Zhengyao and Schmidt, Dominik and Srikanth, Dhruv and Xu, Dixing and Kaplan, Ian and Jacenko, Deniss and Wu, Yuxiang
records.summary: Searches a tree of candidate programs using drafting, debugging, and improvement operators, with a fixed heuristic for parent selection. It is a precursor for search design; its original task-solution search does not itself establish harness self-modification.

records.title: Recursive self-improvement of AI research agents
records.authors: Srikanth, Dhruv and Zhao, Bingchen and Xu, Dixing and Wu, Yuxiang and Jiang, Zhengyao
records.summary: AIDE^2 optimizes a research agent through nested code-search and agent-rewrite loops. The discovered agent changes strategy selection and context management; the main outer driver and incumbent rule remain fixed, with a separate ignition experiment testing an evolved outer driver. That experiment does not establish superior sample efficiency of the evolved improver. Reusing an edited inner codebase is therefore distinguished from automatically replacing the outer rewriter after every update.

records.title: MemoHarness: Agent Harnesses That Learn from Experience
records.authors: Huang, Yue and Wang, Wenjie and Bao, Han and Ma, Yuchen and Luo, Xiaonan and Nian, Yi and Zhuang, Haomin and Liu, Zheyuan and Zhao, Yue and Zhang, Xiangliang
records.summary: Organizes harness experience into per-case records and distilled global patterns. Structured retrieval supports search and case-specific deployment adaptation from a frozen training bank without test-time feedback or extra search rounds.

records.title: Filesystem-Based Memory for LLM Agents: Organization, Evolution, and Sustainability
records.authors: Zhou, Sizhe and Yu, Sheldon and Wei, Hui and Wu, Junda and Ouyang, Siru and Jiao, Yizhu and Pan, Shijia and McAuley, Julian and Zhang, Yu and Yu, Tong and Han, Jiawei
records.category: Memory, Context, Skills, and Experience Reuse
records.summary: Studies management, search, and execution roles around filesystem memory, comparing curated hierarchies, verbatim logs, and chunk retrieval. Organization can reduce retrieval cost without consistently improving correctness, and its sustainability depends on model and tool choices.

records.title: Tree Search for Language Model Agents
records.authors: Koh, Jing Yu and McAleer, Stephen and Fried, Daniel and Salakhutdinov, Ruslan
records.category: Task-Time Search and Output Refinement (Adjacent Work)
records.summary: Applies best-first search over actions in interactive web environments. It provides a task-level search reference for distinguishing planning within one task from search over persistent harness implementations.

records.title: Harness-Zero: Harness Distillation via Agent-as-Harness
records.authors: Ye, Haoran and Lu, Yuxing and Dong, Haonan and Su, Zhaochen and Song, Guojie
records.category: Model and Policy Training, Harness Co-Evolution, and Distillation
records.summary: Uses an agent guided by an optimized harness to review and correct student actions in the target harness action space, then fine-tunes the student on the resulting trajectories. The specialized guidance is removed at deployment. This is harness-to-weight distillation, rather than frozen-model harness editing. The reported experiments cover knowledge work, tool use, and science; the training appendix specifies separate domain-specific fine-tuning runs, so the macro-average is not evidence of one jointly trained universal model.

records.title: Self-Evolving Harness on Multiple Tasks with the Agent as Its Own Optimizer
records.authors: Xu, Qiankai
records.summary: A single-author paper affiliated with Nanjing University. The solver and proposer use the same frozen model and current harness, with the proposer directly editing the code and evolution notes. Evolution mixes five benchmarks, followed by continual adaptation with replay; evaluation includes held-out tasks and five initially unseen benchmarks. Its pretraining/training terminology refers to external harness optimization, not weight updates. Acceptance checks runnability rather than requiring a measured performance improvement. The updated harness is reused by both roles in subsequent iterations, supporting discussion of partial recursion. The execution interface and outer scheduling remain fixed; task-score gains alone do not isolate an improvement in the proposer. This is a central reference for shared solver/proposer harnesses, data mixtures, transfer, and update scheduling.

records.title: DynaHarness: A Dynamic Physical Harness for Self-Evolving Robot Agents
records.authors: Deng, Haoyuan and Liu, Jiebin and Zhang, Tengxiao and Yan, Langning and Cao, Hongye and Wang, Ziwei
records.summary: Connects slower semantic planning with faster physical execution through an explicit execution contract around a frozen VLA. Recorded failures guide changes to reusable capabilities or execution mechanisms, and paired regression checks govern adoption. It supplies a robotics example of failure localization, runtime control, and gated persistent revision; the reported manipulation results do not establish unrestricted self-modification of the optimizer.

records.title: HarnessEvolve: Learning from Reference Trajectories for Reliable Agent Self-Evolution
records.authors: Jiang, Wen and Chu, Mingmin and Tian, Yimeng and Zhang, Qianxin and Yang, Haofei and Yang, Rui and Liu, Yang and Lv, Tao and Li, Fangming
records.summary: Diagnoses failures by aligning agent trajectories with reference trajectories generated using ground-truth answers, then clusters errors into reusable improvement targets. Separate execution, evaluation, optimization, and gating roles support harness edits. Quality screening targets leakage and prompt growth; performance screening checks current and recent batches, with held-out epoch selection. Relevant to diagnostic feedback and retention, but its privileged reference access must be distinguished from label-free self-evaluation.

records.title: A Theory of Reliable Self-Evolution for Agent Harnesses
records.authors: Cai, Qianshu and Zhang, Yonggang and Nie, Jun and Ran, Maohao and Zheng, Huajiang and Song, Jun and Tian, Xinmei and Guo, Yike and Xue, Wei
records.summary: Develops conditions and a validation rule for reliably adopting harness changes while preserving previously successful behavior. It analyzes how verification and evaluation costs limit progress and how observed performance shifts can diagnose stagnation. These are conditional theoretical guarantees, not a universal empirical safety certificate. Version 2, revised September 28, replaces the earlier title Safe Harness Self-Evolution: A Theoretical Analysis of Feasibility and Limits; the two titles denote one paper.

records.title: Harness Evolution as Learning: Approximation, Generalization, and Optimization Limits of Self-Improving Personal Agents
records.authors: Gan, Zeyu and Gong, Zixuan and Liu, Yong
records.summary: Studies personal-agent harness architecture, scale, and evolution algorithms using a preference-oriented benchmark and a learning-theoretic formulation. Approximation, generalization, and optimization errors organize limits imposed by reachable policies, finite evidence, and biased updates. Useful for explaining why larger harnesses or more evolution rounds need not yield better personalization.

records.title: EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement
records.authors: Nie, Jun and Zhang, Yonggang and Cai, Qianshu and Cheung, Yiu-ming and Tian, Xinmei and Han, Bo
records.summary: Distributes a shared harness to deployments that evolve it on local workloads, then combines program adaptations and redistributes the result. Scope-typed, evidence-guided aggregation addresses conflicts between independently edited programs. It directly broadens update integration from selecting one candidate to composing distributed experience. Keeping workloads local is a system design choice, not by itself a formal privacy guarantee.

records.title: SkillOpt: Executive Strategy for Self-Evolving Agent Skills
records.authors: Yang, Yifan and Gong, Ziyang and Huang, Weiquan and Yang, Qihao and Zhou, Ziwei and Huang, Zisu and Li, Yan and Gao, Xuemei and Dai, Qi and Liu, Bei and Qiu, Kai and Yang, Yuqing and Chen, Dongdong and Yang, Xue and Luo, Chong
records.category: Memory, Context, Skills, and Experience Reuse
records.summary: Optimizes a skill document as external state of a frozen agent. A separate optimizer converts scored rollouts into bounded add/delete/replace edits, with strict validation improvement required for acceptance. Edit budgets, rejected-edit memory, and slower epoch-level updates connect it to regularization, memory, and scheduling. It is component-level text optimization rather than evidence that the entire harness or optimizer rewrites itself.

records.title: Skill Issue: Lessons from Optimizing Repository SKILLs for Coding Agents
records.authors: Kozyrev, Mykhailo and Kozyrev, Andrei and Podkopaev, Anton
records.summary: Builds repository-specific optimization tasks from merged pull requests reverted at a fixed base commit and evaluates the incremental value of a skill document. Across three Kotlin repositories, apparent gains from GEPA are not separable from run-to-run variance at the available sample size, while SkillOpt yields little change. It is useful counterevidence to treating a plausible-looking skill or a small score increase as a reliable improvement.

records.title: R^2 Flow: Recursive Self-Improvement via Recursive Skill Evolution
records.authors: Zhang, Mingda and Huang, Qiang and Li, Yanjin and Wang, Zijia and Lin, Qika and Tang, Xiaoying and Shen, Tiesunlong
records.category: Model and Policy Training, Harness Co-Evolution, and Distillation
records.summary: Alternates policy learning, independent verification, and versioned skill-library changes on a shared-state orchestration graph. Separate measures of usage and signed utility prioritize edits, verifier evidence gates them, and a residual-variance plateau controls timing. Library revisions change the graph used by subsequent policy learning. Relevant to coupled learning/evolution, attribution, and scheduling; skill use is explicitly separated from evidence of benefit.

records.title: Recursive Self-Improvement via On-Policy Distillation for Reasoning
records.authors: Yin, Shangjian and Zhao, Zehao and Asadi, Kavosh and Liu, Rui and Lu, Yuchen and Mei, Shike and Cui, Hang and Simon, Luke and Shi, Zhouxing and Firooz, Hamed
records.category: Model and Policy Training, Harness Co-Evolution, and Distillation
records.summary: Updates a privileged teacher alongside a reasoning student and combines this dynamic co-evolution with training on verified concise rewrites. The teacher receives ground-truth context. This is adjacent model-level self-distillation for mathematical reasoning, included to distinguish weight-space recursion from persistent harness revision rather than as direct evidence of harness RSI.

records.title: LiteEvo: Automated, Cost-Efficient Harness Evolution for Generalization to Unseen Tasks
records.authors: Choi, Euntae and Song, Sumin and Yoo, Sungjoo
records.summary: Uses tool-free meta-agents to extract reusable components from execution traces, maintain a versioned library, and compose successive harnesses from a common neutral starting point. It reports both evolution-task results and a separate train/test generalization protocol. Useful for component reuse and optimization cost; sharing a neutral seed across benchmarks should not be confused with evolving one mixed-benchmark harness.

records.title: Recursive Harness Distillation across Agents for Robot Manipulation
records.authors: Kim, Seungyeon and Lee, Junhoo and Kim, Minkyu and Kim, Baekseung and Kwak, Nojun
records.category: Memory, Context, Skills, and Experience Reuse
records.summary: A stronger agent converts intervention experience into a reusable playbook for a lighter robot agent, then revises the playbook using execution feedback. The playbook transfers across agents and manipulation instances without model-weight updates. This is external experience distillation, distinct from the weight distillation of Harness-Zero.

records.title: Agent Harness Distillation: Inference-Time Harness Extraction and Exploitation in Autonomous Multi-Agent Systems
records.authors: Cui, Yu and Yang, Wuli and Shi, Yirui and Xia, Junhao and Jiang, Hui and Gao, Lei and Bao, Chenfu
records.summary: Studies black-box extraction of another agent system's inference-time harness behavior. An initial inferred harness is refined to match target behavior, and a deception-based defense is evaluated. Included as security and intellectual-property context: its use of distillation concerns behavioral extraction, not Harness-Zero's student-weight training or autonomous improvement of one's own harness.

records.title: Automatic Harness Evolution for Hardware Design Verification: Can LLMs Consolidate Gains Across Discovered Harnesses?
records.authors: Seyoum, Kidus and Mittur, Ajay
records.summary: Examines harness evolution around a fixed model on proprietary hardware-verification tasks. Better completion and any-hit coverage do not consistently consolidate into stronger repeatable correctness, and selected validation gains can disappear on replay. A separate repair case study explores cross-benchmark behavior. Relevant to archives, metric choice, regression, and the distinction between complementary specializations and a uniformly better harness.

records.title: The Last Harness You'll Ever Build
records.authors: Seong, Haebin and Yin, Li and Zhang, Haoran and Shi, Zhan
records.summary: Presents a two-level design: an inner worker/evaluator/editor loop improves a task harness, while an outer loop optimizes the evolution blueprint across tasks. This is a direct conceptual reference for making the improvement procedure an optimization target. Its broad domain-adaptation ambition should not itself be treated as proof of general or unbounded RSI.

records.title: Learning from Research: Toward Lifelong Agent Harness Evolution
records.authors: Yang, Jingbo and Lai, Kwei-Herng and Wang, Xiaowen and Harari, Yaar and Gabrilovich, Evgeniy and Chang, Shiyu
records.summary: ScholarEvolve draws proposal ideas from research publications rather than relying only on observed task failures and the editor's existing knowledge. It organizes directions by harness module, identifies strategies with topic modeling, and tests implementations and combinations. AppWorld and Tau2-Bench experiments support its research-guided evolution design; the intended ability to ingest future papers is distinct from demonstrating indefinite improvement.

records.title: Scale and Selection: What Makes Automatic Harness Evolution Work for Visual-Interface Robot Agents
records.authors: Wei, Zhijie and Tan, Ferris and Wang, Jinghui
records.summary: Studies how rollout batch size and candidate selection affect automatically evolved robot-agent harnesses. Larger batches improve the evidence behind promotion, while a strict champion/challenger rule performs better than unconditional acceptance in the reported setting. Relevant to evaluation noise, resource allocation, and regression prevention; repeated use of a fixed selection set remains distinct from held-out assessment.

records.title: EvoGen-Harness: Learning Where and How to Evolve Image-Generation Harnesses
records.authors: Luo, Jiabin and Liu, Yinan and Meng, Chunlei and Guo, Yufei
records.summary: Evolves multiple responsibilities outside a frozen image generator. Trace aggregates stochastic execution evidence, uses failure attribution to prioritize candidate changes, and revisits residual failures as components change. A no-update option and held-out validation constrain adoption. It extends the task taxonomy to image generation and illustrates attribution-guided search; it is not evidence of model-weight training.

records.title: Video-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Understanding Agents via Harness Evolution
records.authors: Luo, Bingjun and Guo, Jialin and Li, Siqi
records.summary: Uses the video agent's own language model to revise its executable observation harness. Active investigation returns to training videos for additional evidence that can distinguish competing failure explanations, rather than relying only on the original trace. Selection considers both answer quality and visual processing cost. It contributes a multimodal example of proposal-time evidence acquisition and cost-aware retention.

records.title: RSIGame: Autonomous Agentic Game Development with Recursive Self-improvement
records.authors: Wu, Wenyi and Fu, Minghao and You, Jieyu and Zhou, Kun and Liu, Siqi and Salvi, Aayush and Lin, Yiheng and Zhang, Ce and Lan, Xiaohan and Zhu, Jiahui and Zhong, Yujie and She, Qi and Huang, Biwei
records.category: Model and Policy Training, Harness Co-Evolution, and Distillation
records.summary: Combines local exploration, diagnosis, and game revision with a global checkpoint and regression-monitoring loop. An evolving checklist carries testing guidance, and successful development experience is subsequently internalized through training. Included as an application and hybrid-learning reference: revisions to a generated game must be distinguished from revisions to the reusable improvement harness.

records.title: Schema: Discovering Unknown Environments via Agentic Program Induction
records.authors: Zeng, Guanning and Wang, Jiani and Ma, Wenjie and Yin, Shaofeng and Wang, Chenyang and Liu, Shichen and Kanazawa, Angjoo and Ni, Wode and Li, Xiuyu and Zanette, Andrea and Feng, Haiwen
records.summary: Maintains an executable program workspace representing learned environment rules. Interfaces check programs against interaction history, support planning, and verify execution step by step. It is relevant infrastructure for structured experience and environment discovery; revising an environment model within the harness is not automatically revision of the harness optimizer.

records.title: ActiveSaddler: Automated Curriculum Learning for Agent Harness Optimization
records.authors: Park, Sungho and Kim, Wonjoong and Zhang, Jue and Han, Wook-Shin and Gao, Pengfei and Park, Chanyoung and Yao, Yongqiang and Fu, Rao and Nallipogu, Elsie and Lin, Qingwei and Rühle, Victor
records.summary: Adapts the training curriculum alongside the harness through a non-stationary bandit. Recurrent failures create reusable pattern arms, estimated learning progress changes their priority, and exploration discovers new targets. GAIA2 and Terminal-Bench experiments compare it with the same harness optimizer under a fixed scenario order. It directly informs search, task selection, and experiment allocation; adaptive curriculum control is not necessarily self-rewriting controller code.

records.title: NavHarness: Towards Lifelong Embodied Navigation
records.authors: Zhao, Xunyi and Zhou, Jian and Lin, Sihao and Zhou, Gengze and Li, Zerui and Yan, Xinyu and Liu, Jiajun and van den Hengel, Anton and Wu, Qi
records.category: Memory, Context, Skills, and Experience Reuse
records.summary: Carries maps, task records, and house knowledge between navigation sessions, checking them against new observations and consolidating corrections. Structured recovery handovers and outcome summaries support later reuse without weight training. It provides a recent embodied-memory example, with the distinction that accumulating or correcting task experience does not by itself demonstrate an evolving optimizer.

records.title: Co-Evolving Harnesses and Models: On-Policy Correction Helps Weaker Models Catch Up Where Imitation Fails
records.authors: Yu, Zhou and Bi, Bin and Pentyala, Shiva Kumar and Mehrotra, Shubham and Chaudhuri, Sougata and Bhagavath, Shilpa and Chen, Zeyuan and Xu, Ran and Mui, Phil and Zhu, James and Asur, Sitaram
records.category: Model and Policy Training, Harness Co-Evolution, and Distillation
records.summary: Finds that copying full expert trajectories can degrade a weaker model operating under its evolved harness. It instead identifies a failing turn in the weaker model's own rollout and requests a localized expert correction for training. The enterprise-task study makes model–harness compatibility a concrete issue in joint evolution, rather than assuming weight and harness improvements add independently.

records.title: How Much of a Harness Does a Strong Agent Need for Autonomous ML Engineering?
records.authors: Brilliantov, Kirill and Hernández-Cano, Alejandro and Abbé, Emmanuel
records.summary: Compares elaborate open-source MLE harnesses with a minimal coding-agent session using the same frontier model and time budget. The evaluated systems do not outperform the minimal baseline, and ablations question the value of extra orchestration in those settings. Relevant to budget-matched baselines and complexity; the conclusion is specific to the studied MLE tasks, not a universal rejection of harness engineering.

records.title: Co-Harness: Co-Evolving Harnesses and Model Weights for LLM Agents
records.authors: Chen, Zhengyu and Xiao, Teng and Zhu, Huaisheng and Yuan, Yige and Zhang, Luan and Wang, Jingang
records.category: Model and Policy Training, Harness Co-Evolution, and Distillation
records.summary: Alternates harness optimization with model fine-tuning for AI research agents. A HarnessCritic diagnoses failed trajectories and proposes validated local changes; the updated harness generates trajectories for subsequent weight updates. It is a direct joint-optimization reference, useful for contrasting co-evolution with one-way harness distillation and purely frozen-model harness search.

records.title: HARBOR: Automated Harness Optimization
records.authors: Sengupta, Biswa and Wang, Jinhua
records.summary: Formulates harness configuration as constrained noisy Bayesian optimization over a bounded mixed-variable space. A structured surrogate, cost-aware multi-fidelity acquisition, trust regions, and a posterior safety constraint select configurations. It expands the search taxonomy beyond LLM-authored edits and trees, while remaining configuration optimization under a specified search procedure.

records.title: SCLATE: a Substrate for Continual-Learning Agent Training and Evaluation
records.authors: Jung, Youngmok and Salekin, Sirajul and Tran, Henry and Movellan, Javier and Huang, Zhao and Bilkhu, Manjot
records.summary: Provides a shared event scheduler for benchmark events and agent-side activity such as session changes and memory consolidation. Its rollout engine supports unmodified harnesses and memory systems, enabling controlled comparisons and model post-training. Relevant to scheduling and evaluation infrastructure; its weight-training results should not be described as autonomous harness-code evolution.

records.title: LongHorizon-Harness: Advancing Long-Horizon Agents for Real-World Tasks
records.authors: Ma, Ziyu and Huang, Hailang and Zou, Shun and Wang, Yong and Yang, Shidong and Hu, Yiming and Wei, Fei and Chu, XiangXiang
records.summary: Uses a Manage–Execute–Audit loop with external task state, fresh executor contexts, and a read-only auditor that checks environment facts. Adapters support different models and existing agent backends. Included as harness architecture and verification context; improving execution through this fixed organization is distinct from automatically evolving the organization itself.

records.title: MemCodex: Self-Programming Hierarchical Memory for Language Agents
records.authors: Wang, Xiaoqiang and Liu, Bang
records.category: Memory, Context, Skills, and Experience Reuse
records.summary: Rewrites executable memory-layer programs governing construction, indexing, retrieval, and routing. Hierarchical reads proceed from coarse to fine and can fall back to original history. This is directly relevant to evolution of the memory-management procedure, rather than only accumulation of memory contents. The preprint is marked work in progress.

records.title: GenMem: Generative Symbolic Memory for Self-Evolving Harness
records.authors: Jiang, Xinke and Feng, Tao and Xu, Weixuan and Zhang, Zhixin and Yang, Zhibang and Zhang, Wentao and Zhu, Runchuan and Chu, Xu and Zhao, Junfeng and Wang, Yasha
records.category: Memory, Context, Skills, and Experience Reuse
records.summary: Uses stable symbolic identifiers to address memories whose contents can change. A retriever and an evolver learn memory access and revision through GRPO with process and outcome rewards. Relevant to memory addressing and learned management policies; its training component should not be described as purely weight-frozen harness search.

records.title: CHIME: Credit-Aware Hierarchical Memory Evolution for Long-Horizon Agentic Planning
records.authors: Ye, Yongshi and Lan, Tian and Jiang, Feihu and Ye, Muyang and Zhu, Bin and Jia, Qianghuai and Wang, Longyue and Xu, Zhao and Luo, Weihua and Shi, Xiaodong
records.category: Memory, Context, Skills, and Experience Reuse
records.summary: Separates planning memory from execution memory. Before storing experience, it attributes outcomes to planning, execution, both, or neither, then updates the corresponding bank. It supports discussion of credit assignment and selective memory updates without parameter training; outcome attribution should not be equated with an independently established causal effect.

records.title: Self-Evolving Search Index
records.authors: Lee, Sangam and Lee, Wonjae and Kim, Sunghwan and Kim, Deogyong and Kim, Jaehoon and Nam, Daye and Kang, SeongKu and Lee, Dongha
records.category: Memory, Context, Skills, and Experience Reuse
records.summary: SELF-INDEX diagnoses retrieval failures, selectively revises document index keys, and validates revisions before updating the index. This supplies a concrete example of evolving the retrieval substrate. It is adjacent to harness memory management, not evidence that the complete agent or its optimizer recursively modifies itself.

records.title: COBRA-Skills: Contextual Bandit-Guided Evolution for Agent Skill Optimization
records.authors: Lu, Pingchen and Wang, Xiangyi and Li, Xiang and Mao, Jie and Qu, Zikun and Luo, Junfeng and Shu, Yao and Low, Bryan Kian Hsiang and Dai, Zhongxiang
records.summary: Formulates skill optimization as budgeted sequential optimization over an evolving candidate population. Contextual bandits prioritize informative or promising evaluations, while execution feedback guides skill revision. It connects search organization to evaluation-budget allocation; the editable objects are reusable skills, not necessarily the entire runtime harness.

records.title: SAGE: A Statistical Acceptance Gate for Self-Evolving Agents
records.authors: Wang, Yihao and Xia, Linhan and Liu, Rui and Zhang, Zhaofeng and Wu, Hongyu and Yang, Yang and He, Jinglu and Guo, Yu and Lei, Kai
records.summary: Compares candidate and incumbent skills on the same validation items. Acceptance requires positive regression-weighted gain, a one-sided paired significance test against the corresponding break-even threshold, and a cap on the fraction of previously solved items that regress. This SAGE is the statistical-gate paper, distinct from other methods with the same acronym.

records.title: SBCO: Self-Supervised, Verifier-Grounded Harness Optimization For Planning Agents
records.authors: Kulkarni, Vivek and Paul, Sudipta and Kumar, Aounon and Tzou, Nicholas and Chappidi, Srinivas
records.summary: Alternates improvements to a decomposed verifier bank and a harness policy through approximate block-coordinate ascent for constrained planning. The meta-agent remains fixed. This is a useful evaluator–policy optimization example and a boundary case separating closed-loop harness improvement from recursive modification of the optimizer.

records.title: SelfOp: An Optimization Algorithm for Self-Improving Security Agents
records.authors: Ullah, Saad and Kaya, Yigitcan and Kruegel, Christopher and Vigna, Giovanni and Stringhini, Gianluca
records.summary: Aggregates textual error signals across instances to revise instructions, skills, and reference documents, using cross-instance consensus and a gradient-signal stopping rule. The authors explicitly keep the execution harness and model weights fixed. It belongs in contextual proposal and skill optimization, with this narrower editable scope stated explicitly.

records.title: Breaking the Environment Wall: Evolving LLM Agent Environments for Recursive Self-Improvement
records.authors: Wu, Yukai and Yang, Yuanjing and Zhou, Le and Han, Shaokun and Wang, Haoyu and Tang, Zirui and Zheng, Weihuang and Pan, Maxm and Zhou, Xuanhe and Wu, Fan
records.summary: Env-Rethink organizes files and evidence through collection maps and event logs, uses a post-trained model to identify environmental noise, and produces changed environments through virtual event histories. This is related environment preparation and evolution, not interchangeable with editing the task-agent harness. This entry records version 1 and its title.

records.title: Auto-RecSys: Harnessing Autonomous Research Agents for Industry-Scale Recommender System
records.authors: Li, Ming and Li, Dai and Ning, Xuying and Sun, Bo and Li, Rui and Zhang, Yi and Gong, Silvia and Cao, Xuan and Li, Rui and Carapcea, Cornelia and Zhang, Qunshu and Wang, Zhigang and Xia, Yinglong and Wang, Andy
records.summary: Combines asynchronous experiments, shared cross-server memory, and separation of natural-language skills from deterministic execution scripts. Execution playbooks retain operational experience while an idea loop uses experimental results to guide future proposals. It supports experiment-management and experience-reuse discussions; two loops alone do not establish recursive optimizer evolution.

records.title: SEABench: Benchmarking Endogenous Misalignment In Self-Evolving Agents
records.authors: Das, Saswat and Viswanathan, Parvati and Donnelly, Daniel and Huang, Chang and Abdelnabi, Sahar and Fioretto, Ferdinando
records.summary: Evaluates safety failures emerging from persistent self-evolution across 48 longitudinal task sequences involving instructions, memory protocols, tools, and skills. Paired non-evolving agents support attribution of failures to evolution. Relevant to long-term safety evaluation across update surfaces rather than only immediate task-score gains.

records.title: LLM-as-a-Judge Is Not an Oracle: Why Self-Improving Agents Need Deterministic Guardrails
records.authors: Wahi, Vansh
records.summary: A position and system report describing evaluation failures in prompt-optimization loops and the PROCTOR architecture. Deterministic gates, role separation, isolated evaluation, frozen holdouts, and canary cases constrain judge-driven updates. Use as a reported design and failure analysis, not a general proof that these safeguards eliminate reward hacking.

records.title: Cost-Aware Optimization for Agentic Query Execution
records.authors: Nie, Lunyiu and Xia, Yilin and Liu, Yiren and Jermaine, Christopher and Chaudhuri, Swarat
records.summary: EnumGRPO enumerates agentic query-plan choices and converts quality–cost feedback into reusable planning heuristics through in-context reinforcement learning. It extends workflow-optimization coverage to database queries and cost-aware planning; the term reinforcement learning here should not by itself imply model-weight updates.

records.authors: Jana, Prithwish and Goswami, Mononito and Liu, Hao and Li, Xinyu and Huang, Langlin and Huang, Zhehui and Huang, Zhishen and Blöbaum, Patrick and Deoras, Anoop and Jain, Purak and Kanakaris, Nikos and Genc, Sahika
records.summary: Evolves complete agent harnesses using island-based lineage trees, per-island mutators, and an orchestrator. The history retains rejected mutations as negative evidence. This connects harness search with adaptation of its search configuration. The specified orchestration actions do not by themselves establish recursive rewriting of the orchestrator; capability-level claims require that distinction.
